newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Japan promises transparency on security pact - China.
newsitem.headline: Japan promises transparency on security pact - China.

text.p: Japan has promised China it will be more transparent regarding its security pact with the United States, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen and Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda held talks in Hong Kong, where the two are attending the ceremony marking the British colony's handover to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
"The two sides have discussed the Japan/U.S. security pact," Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news conference.
"Japanese Foreign Minister Mr Ikeda indicated that in the future both Japan and the United States should maintain a certain degree of transparency in this regard," he said.

Washington and Tokyo earlier this month unveiled new plans to revamp their strategic relationship and widen potential military cooperation -- always a highly sensitive issue for China, which suffered hugely under the Japanese military in the 1930s and 1940s.
The move prompted China to warn Tokyo to act carefully to avoid destabilising the Asia-Pacific region with moves to boost its military profile.

Shen also said Qian and Ikeda did not specifically discuss the case of islands claimed by both Japan and China, but the two sides agreed they should take measures to contain troublesome elements in relations and develop positive aspects.

The disputed islands in the East China Sea, administered by Tokyo, are called the Diaoyus by China and Taiwan and the Senkakus by Japan. Recent landings on them by Japanese right-wingers have outraged activists in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
